stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $PQRS$ with diagonals $PR$ and $QS$ meeting at $O$. Diya already knows $PR=QS$ and that the diagonals bisect each other, as in a rectangle. She asks what extra diagonal condition makes $PQRS$ a square.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: The diagonals must also meet at right angles at $O$, so $PQRS$ is a square.
Call the extra condition the word diagonal and treat that label alone as the square test.
Equal diagonals that bisect each other and meet at right angles classify $PQRS$ as a square.
A kite test with one symmetry diagonal alone turns the rectangle construction into a square.

teacher.key_rationale: Rectangle diagonals that also meet at right angles give a square; A and C state that extra condition. B substitutes the topic label. D conflates a kite test with the square diagonal condition.
